title: Pilot weekly lab checkpoint - throughput & latency dual-compare (NimbleMed)
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review lab benchmark results comparing Redwood inference against the incumbent provider. Reviewed median and tail latency, throughput at target concurrency, and cost tradeoffs. Identified routing/quantization tuning to reduce p95 tail and a plan to request dedicated slots for a sustained throughput test. Customer requested SOC2 + SAML docs and a short POC checklist for on-prem validation.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Recording id: ff-20270119-9b3a
Attendees: Grace Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortega (Redwood SE), Tanya Patel (Redwood CSM), Alex Chen (NimbleMed CTO), Priya Rao (ML Platform), Samir Desai (SRE), Jenna Morris (Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be noisy): Reviewed bench runs, Redwood p50 better than incumbent, p95 close, noted KV cache miss in tail; plan for dedicated slot stress test and to share security docs.

[00:00] Grace (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick agenda: walk results from last 48h lab runs, talk tuning, and agree next steps. can everyone see the shared spreadsheet link? (link posted in chat)
[00:18] Alex (NimbleMed): Yep seeing it. thanks. we did a quick glance earlier, looks promising but some p95 spikes we need to understand.
[00:32] Marcus (Redwood SE): quick context — we replayed your baseline workload against Redwood hosted and Redwood Dedicaed instance (note: host name typed as Dedicaed in notes), and the incumbent vendor snapshot you gave us. we captured p50/p95/p99, throughput at 10/25/50 concurrency, and token/s metrics.
[01:05] Priya (NimbleMed): thanks marcus. can you highlight the headline numbers first? p50 and p95?
[01:12] Marcus (Redwood SE): sure. for the 8k prompt set: incumbent p50 ~ 120ms, redwood-hosted p50 ~ 98ms, redwood-dedicated p50 ~ 92ms. p95 incumbent 380ms, redwood-hosted 220ms, redwood-dedicated 175ms. p99 we saw incumb 1.2s, redwood-dedicated ~520ms. throughput at 50 concurrent: incumbent capped at ~95 req/s before queueing, redwood-dedicated sustained ~142 req/s at same token distribution.
[01:50] Jenna (Product): wow thats a big throughput delta. is cost accounted?
[01:55] Grace (Redwood): yes we included approximate token cost delta in the sheet. note that dedicated slot pricing is different model — committed capacity. we'll send the procurement sheet.
[02:10] Samir (SRE): those p99 numbers look better on you but still 520ms might be high for a few of our user flows. we care about tail latency for interactive agents. what's causing the spikes?
[02:21] Marcus (Redwood SE): two things: one, KV cache warmup and prefix cache misses — in some of the replays certain session prefixes weren't matching so we dropped to full generation path. two, occasional background eviction on the node during peak which bumped some tail. we saw hints of disco I/O pause during one run (disk/io telemetry), might be infra scheduling in the shared host. on Dedicated runs that tail drops pretty consistently.
[02:55] Alex (NimbleMed): can you explain the KV cache thing, i've seen docs but not fully clear.
[03:03] Marcus (Redwood SE): yeah, KV cache is per-session key/value for decoder states — if prefix hash mismatches or request routing sends to different host, we can't reuse the cache. we have prefix sticky routing and also an auto-kv pref adapter. in some runs routing didn't keep affinity because of burst autoscale, so we lost reuse. note I typed prefix adapter as "pref adapter" in notes.
[03:36] Priya (ML Platform): ok so is the routing fix something we can control on our side (client) or you do it server side?
[03:43] Grace (Redwood): it's a mix — we can set routing policies (affinity by session id) and also enable our sticky prefix routing on the dedicated cluster. we recommended enabling 'session_affinity: true' in the SDK for these flows. we'll add a sample patch.
[03:58] [04:00] Marcus (Redwood SE): also quantization choices impacted latency/cost. we tested the 4-bit quantized variant for one model to push throughput — that reduced p50 by another ~12% but a small amount of QA drift on few prompts.
[04:22] Jenna (Product): can you show an example of the QA drift? is it acceptable?
[04:28] Marcus (Redwood SE): we flagged 7 prompts with safe-regression checks — mostly shorter rewrites that lost nuance. i'll attach the diff lines. clearly acceptable for some bulk tasks but not for high-trust UI without additional eval gating.
[04:48] Alex (CTO): for our main interactive assist flow we can't tolerate those regressions, so quantization is only for low-risk background jobs. agree?
[04:55] Priya (ML Platform): agree. but we do want to test quantized path for notification batchers.
[05:05] Grace (Redwood): good split — we can route sensitive flow to full precision and background to quantized. that's where routing/fallback policies help.
[05:14] [05:20] Samir (SRE): on the infra side, if we request dedicated slots what does that guarantee? we need predictable tail latency and no noisy neighbor.
[05:29] Grace (Redwood): Dedicated is reserved gpu pools with commit; you get placement isolation and we can pin the model to specific instances. SLA and reserved capacity pricing will be in the procurement doc.
[05:42] Samir (SRE): we will want JIT scaling off, and low-noise neighbor assurances.
[05:48] Marcus (Redwood SE): yep we can set scaling policy to manual for the dedicated test and isolate to a single rack. we'll provide the metrics streams for node-level telemetry.
[06:00] [06:10] Priya (ML Platform): ok things i noted: 1) routing affinity changes, 2) quantization guardrails, 3) dedicated slot stress test. can we do an extended run to reproduce p99 pathology?
[06:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes — plan is 2 hour run at 50 concurrent using your prompt set and 30% longer sessions to exercise KV cache. we'll capture KV hit rates, cpu/gpu util, kernel latencies.
[06:40] Alex (CTO): timeline? we need data for our internal architecture review next week.
[06:46] Grace (Redwood): we'll kick the run this Friday (2027-01-22) and share logs and summarized p50/p95/p99 by Monday EOD 2027-01-24.
[06:56] [07:00] Jenna (Product): quick question — how comparable are the baseline settings? are you running same sequence length and all tokens?
[07:07] Marcus (Redwood SE): we mirrored seq len distribution from your production trace and used the exact prompt payloads you gave; the only variance is the incumbent was run in their published config which is slightly different on batching settings, but we note that in the sheet.
[07:24] Priya (ML Platform): i see a note that batch size differences could account for ~10% of throughput delta. can we calibrate that?
[07:32] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes we can run a parity test matching batching/auto-batching flags. also mention kv cache warm-up sequences to make it apples-to-apples.
[07:44] [08:00] Conversation drift / minor crosstalk
[08:05] Alex (NimbleMed): related to security — can you send SOC2 and SAML integration guide? our compliance team will want those before we move to dedicated.
[08:13] Grace (Redwood): yup i'll send SOC2 + SAML docs after this meeting. also our KMS integration doc for customer-managed keys (if you want on-prem or VPC private deployment).
[08:28] Samir (SRE): for on-prem option, do you support HSM?
[08:33] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes HSM via KMS/HSM integrations, note some HSM vendor names got garbled in notes but we support major providers. we'll share the exact compatibility matrix in the doc.
[08:45] [09:00] Marcus (Redwood SE): back to tail — we also saw a small percent of requests routed to fallback model during capacity spikes. our fallback policy tunes by latency and cost; we can prefer a smaller model for low-risk traffic and auto-fallback to full model on errors.
[09:20] Priya (ML Platform): how does the fallback affect cache locality? if a request falls back to different model, do we lose state?
[09:27] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes different model implies different kv shapes; we treat fallback as a best-effort, in high-affinity flows you want to avoid fallback for interactive sessions. that's why we propose sticky routing for those sessions.
[09:40] [10:00] Grace (Redwood): actionables — we'll run stress test, attach raw logs, and price dedicated. also we will provide a sample SDK patch to enable session_affinity and a small guide for pref cache tuning.
[10:15] Alex (CTO): good. one more ask — can you run a direct comparison where you disable quant and use exactly the incumbent batch settings to isolate infra difference?
[10:24] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes that's in scope for parity run. we'll schedule it in the extended test.
[10:33] [11:00] Short pause then Q&A
[11:08] Jenna (Product): small UX question — we saw a 12% improvement on p50 with quant; is streaming affected?
[11:14] Marcus (Redwood SE): streaming latency is slightly better because token generation is faster, but if quantization changes tokenization result for structured output it can cause parse errors; we flagged those in the QA diffs. small risk.
[11:30] [12:00] Priya (ML Platform): can we talk about observability? we want per-route token-level cost and tracer for tail requests.
[12:08] Grace (Redwood): Redwood Console exposes per-route token spend and tracer hooks. for Dedicated we can give longer retention and per-token traces for the pilot.
[12:25] Samir (SRE): we'll need log forwarding and prometheus metrics; can you enable push to our observability stack?
[12:33] Marcus (Redwood SE): yes we can push metrics, and we support prometheus scrape endpoint or pushgateway. we'll outline config in the doc.
[12:45] [13:00] Final recap
[13:04] Grace (Redwood): recap: 1) we saw median and tail improvements vs incumbent, dedicated improves tail further; 2) root causes for residual tail: kv cache misses and host-level evictions during shared runs; 3) plan: parity stress run + 2h dedicated stress run, share logs and price + SOC2/SAML docs.
[13:26] Alex (CTO): sounds good. expecting your doc by Friday.
[13:31] Grace (Redwood): i'll follow up in email and slack with links. thanks everyone.
[13:38] Meeting ends.

Notes (imperfect): some names/acronyms may be mis-transcribed (Dedicaed = Dedicated, KV chaache = KV cache). timestamps approximate.
